title: Six mana: the five-drop and a mana source, not one without the other
briefing: P1 has six lands and holds Mind Stone ({2}, taps for {1}), Serra Angel ({3}{W}{W}) and Llanowar Elves ({G}). Two lines use every mana and leave the Angel plus a mana source on the table: Mind Stone first, tapped at once to help pay for the Angel, or the Angel and the Elves. Casting the Angel and stopping wastes a mana and a card; casting the two small spells leaves the Angel in hand. Mind Stone after the Angel is impossible: one land is left and it costs two.

reference.analysis: Six lands. Mind Stone (2) leaves four lands and taps for one more: five mana, exactly Serra Angel. Or Serra Angel (five lands) and Llanowar Elves (the sixth, a Forest): six mana, exactly. Either way P1 ends with the Angel and a mana source and has seven mana next turn; the only difference is whether the one-mana or the two-mana card stays in hand. All three cannot be cast (eight mana needed, seven available). The Angel alone leaves a mana unused, and the Elves plus Mind Stone leave the Angel in hand.
